newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: AUSTRALIAN STOCKS END WEAKER, BUT OFF LOWS.
newsitem.headline: AUSTRALIAN STOCKS END WEAKER, BUT OFF LOWS.

text.p: SPI futures 2631.0 -18.0 US 30yr cl 6.68 +0.04
10yrbond futs 93.185 -0.020 Gold NY 324.80 Lon fix 326.10
AUD US$0.7450 (Tue $0.7394) CRB Index cl 243.09 -0.66
*Stocks close weaker but recover from lows as market reacts to sharemarket fall in the U.S. Volume 473.49 million, value A$908.82 million, 1,106 stocks traded, 302 steady, 190 up, 614 down
The Australian share market took its lead on Wednesday from a tumble on Wall Street, falling sharply in early trading before ending off its lows.

The All Ordinaries Index closed down 26.9 points, or 1.01 percent, at 2,623.6 after dipping at one stage to just below 2,605. The share price index futurces contract was down 18 points, at 2,631, a 7.4 point premium to the physical market.

"The market opened with the futures down about 26 and we retained that bearish tone all day," said Mark Fordree of ANZ Securities in Sydney. "I don't think we can read too much more into it than that."
Australia was at a different interest rate stage to the U.S, still talking about a rate fall rather than a rise, Fordree said.
"But there's no doubt that if fund managers believe the Dow is in for a protracted recession they will look to lock in some of the equity performance achieved this year," he said.
The Commonwealth Bank ended down just nine cents at A$16.28 after releasing its annual result, a net profit of A$1.078 billion for the year to June 30, compared with A$1.119 billion a year earlier.
CBA shares hit of A$16.02 at one point as the bank warned pressure on margins would continue, but brokers said an increased final dividend and share buy-back plan were positive.
Other bank shares also recovered from early losses, particularly the ANZ, which rebounded 34 cents to end up four cents at A$10.04.
Coca-Cola Amatil continued to show the recent volatility of its share price, slipping 55 cents to A$14.185.
The soft drink bottler has declined since several profit downgrades after last week's flat interim profit result.
The share price has eased since a number of profit downgrades in the wake of last week's steady interim result.
Retailer Coles Myer slipped six cents to A$6.40, while Woolworths fell 14 cents to A$4.16.
However, other blue chips held their own.
Market leader BHP rallied to close up 11 cents, while Qantas ended down just one cent at A$2.99 on turnover of 3.5 million shares.
About 5.4 million Burns Philp shares changed hands, including 4.56 million, about 0.9 percent of the issued capital, specialled by Deutsche Morgan Grenfell at A$2.42.
Dealers said BHP's rally followed the release of results by WMC Ltd, which were in line with market expectations at A$228.2 million before abnormals, down 40.9 percent.
The WMC result was welcomed by the market which pushed the share price higher before it settled down one cent at A$7.41.
Metal Manufactures, which reported a sharp fall in interim net profit but forecast an improved second half, closed down nine cents at A$3.06.
In the local bond market, the long-end recovered early losses, with the 10-year Australian bond yield up a point at 6.83 percent.
The Australian dollar rallied through resistance levels to US$0.7455 by 4.45 p.m. (0645 GMT), over half a cent up on its early US$0.7403 and Tuesday's US$0.7393.
